problem_text:
An organizer must allocate a collection of rare books into identical archival boxes for secure transport. The volumes are as follows:

* Tome Alpha: mass 45 units
* Tome Beta: mass 47 units
* Tome Gamma: mass 41 units
* Tome Delta: mass 56 units
* Tome Epsilon: mass 34 units
* Tome Zeta: mass 66 units
* Tome Eta: mass 58 units
* Tome Theta: mass 45 units
* Tome Iota: mass 58 units
* Tome Kappa: mass 62 units
* Tome Lambda: mass 36 units
* Tome Mu: mass 42 units
* Tome Nu: mass 40 units
* Tome Xi: mass 58 units
* Tome Omicron: mass 34 units
* Tome Pi: mass 57 units
* Tome Rho: mass 70 units
* Tome Sigma: mass 55 units
* Tome Tau: mass 47 units

Each archival box can safely support a maximum load of 100 units. The objective is to place every volume into a box, ensuring no box exceeds its load capacity, while minimizing the total number of boxes employed. Each book must be assigned to precisely one box.
